lead: Lanes of houses with courtyards, a park with views and the feel of a summer village in the middle of the city.
text: Around 1870 the first villas of Barcelona's bourgeoisie went up here, as they used it as a summer retreat. El Farró takes its name from Silvestre Farró, who built the first houses in the early 19th century, and in 2007 the two areas were merged into a single neighbourhood.

Its character lies in the Parc del Putxet, which covers a good part of its surface, and in lanes such as Passatge de Sant Felip and Passatge de Mulet, with low-rise houses with courtyards and rows of terraced houses, often built around villas in a colonial or Modernista style. At 1,202 €/month, it has the lowest average rent in the district.
housing: Low-rise houses with courtyards, lanes of terraced houses and low-rise buildings.
